definition.def: If something is confined to a particular place, it exists only in that place. If it is confined to a particular group, only members of that group have it.
examples: The problem is not confined to Germany. [+ to]
These dangers are not confined to smokers. [+ to]

definition.def: A confined space or area is small and enclosed by walls.
examples: His long legs bent up in the confined space.

definition.def: If someone is confined to a wheelchair, bed, or house, they have to stay there, because they have a disability or are ill. This use could cause offence.
examples: He had been confined to a wheelchair since childhood. [+ to]

definition.def: To confine something to a particular place or group means to prevent it from spreading beyond that place or group.
examples: Health officials have successfully confined the epidemic to the Tabatinga area. [VERB noun + to]
The U.S. will soon be taking steps to confine the conflict. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you confine yourself or your activities to something, you do only that thing and are involved with nothing else.
examples: He did not confine himself to the one language. [VERB pronoun-reflexive + to]
Yoko had largely confined her activities to the world of big business. [VERB noun to noun]
His genius was not confined to the decoration of buildings. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If someone is confined to a place such as a prison, they are sent there and are not allowed to leave for a period of time.
examples: He was confined to a prison hospital in Missouri. [be VERB-ed + to]
He announced that the army and police had been confined to barracks. [be V-ed to n]

definition.def: Something that is within the confines of an area or place is within the boundaries enclosing it. [formal]
examples: The movie is set entirely within the confines of the abandoned factory. [+ of]
...the wild grass and weeds that grew in the confines of the grandstand.

definition.def: The confines of a situation, system, or activity are the limits or restrictions it involves.
examples: ...away from the confines of the British class system. [+ of]
I can't stand the confines of this marriage. [+ of]

examples.sentence: In this book about the exploration of the earth's surface, I have confined myself to those whose travels were real and who also aimed at more than personal discovery.
Life has always been confined to corridors and islands here.
Although the technology to create these tunnels existed, steam locomotives could not be used in such a confined space.
Those confined to particular geographical areas, such as countries bordering the Mediterranean or the Nordic countries therefore had to be discarded.
Since some species are largely nocturnal, collecting should not be confined to daytime.
When he became president of the American Psychological Association in 1915, he 'had never even studied a single human being': his research had been confined to experiments on white rats.
And it certainly hasn't been confined to the United States.
By the time European colonisers arrived in the early 1800s, kākāpō had become confined to the central North Island and forested parts of the South Island.
Plumbers may spend much of their time working in confined spaces, where they are at risk from contaminants, including airborne gases, vapours and dusts, that may cause injury from fire or explosion.
Another potential hazard for plumbers in confined spaces is that of drowning, if water sources are not adequately cut off.
